'''Shauraseni Prakrit''' ({{langx|sa|शौरसेनी प्राकृत}}, {{IAST3|Śaurasenī Prākṛta}}, {{IPA|sa|ɕɐurɐseːniː praːkr̩t̪ɐ}}) was a [[Middle Indo-Aryan language]] and a [[Dramatic Prakrit]]. Shauraseni was the chief [[language]] used in drama in [[middle kingdoms of India|medieval]] [[North India|northern India]]. Most of the material in this language originates from the 3rd to 10th centuries, and represented a regional language variety with minor modifications to the same linguistic substratum as other Dramatic Prakrit varieties.<ref name="ollett">{{cite book |last=Ollett |first=Andrew |title=Language of the Snakes: Prakrit, Sanskrit, and the Language Order of Premodern India |chapter=5: Figuring Prakrit |chapter-url=https://www.luminosoa.org/chapters/m/10.1525/luminos.37.e |doi=10.1525/luminos.37.e |date=2017-10-10 |pp=111-140 |isbn=978-0-520-96881-3}} {{Q|Q120550567}}.</ref> 

Among the [[Prakrit]]s, Shauraseni is said to be the one most closely related to [[Classical Sanskrit]] in that it "is derived from the Old Indian Indo-Aryan dialect of the [[Madhyadesa|Madhyadeśa]] on which Classical Sanskrit was mainly based."<ref name="woolner">{{cite web|last1=Woolner|first1=Alfred C.|title=Introduction to Prakrit|url=https://archive.org/details/introductiontopr00woolrich|publisher=University of the Punjab|accessdate=2 March 2016|location=Calcutta}}</ref>{{rp|3-4}} Its descendants include [[Punjabi language|Punjabi]], [[Saraiki language|Saraiki]], [[Hindko]], [[Pahari-Pothwari]], [[Sindhi language|Sindhi]], [[Gujarati languages|Gujarati]], [[Rajasthani languages|Rajasthani]], and [[Hindi]]/[[Urdu]].  <ref>{{Cite book |last=Mesthrie |first=Rajend |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=eUEiEAAAQBAJ&dq=en&pg=PA15 |title=Language in Indenture: A Sociolinguistic History of Bhojpuri-Hindi in South Africa |date=2018-09-14 |publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-0-429-78579-5 |pages=15 |language=en |quote=The outer languages descend from various sources: The Eastern group from Magadhi Prakrit, Marathi from Maharastri Prakrit (which was a sub-division of Ardha-Māgadhi Prakrit, leaning more towards Māgadhi than Śauraseni), while Sindhi and Lahnda, whose early histories are not entirely clear, seem to be derived from Apabhramsas which show Śauraseni influence.}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=HmfEEAAAQBAJ|title=Window to Ancient India : A Tryst with Ancient Science & Philosophy Part II : Languages, Linguistic Systems and Indian Logic System vis-a-vis the Greeks|page=68|first=Satish|last=Joglekar|date=10 June 2023 |publisher=StoryMirror Infotech Pvt |isbn=978-93-90267-91-0 }}</ref>
